facts.raw_span: 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque
no previous history of trauma or any other systemic symptoms
nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
No local lymphadenopathy was observed
Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV: Negative
Hepatitis B: Negative
Hepatitis C: Negative
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits

concepts.why: The patient's lesion is consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, given the vascular proliferation and endothelial cell positivity for CD31, CD34, and D2-40.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with hemangioma, given the vascular proliferation and presence of hemosiderin deposits.
The patient's lesion could also be angiosarcoma, given the vascular proliferation and low proliferation index of endothelial cells.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with verrucous hemangioma, given the presence of hemosiderin deposits and vascular proliferation.
The patient's lesion could also be dermatofibroma, given the absence of systemic symptoms and lack of lymphadenopathy.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with Stewart-Treves syndrome, given the absence of HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C infections.

The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border and the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation with hemosiderin deposits are consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

rationales.F01: The 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque is more typical of a benign vascular lesion such as Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
rationales.F03: The nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis is more typical of a benign vascular lesion such as Hemangioma or Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
rationales.F05: The positivity for CD31, CD34, and D2-40 is more typical of a benign vascular lesion such as Hemangioma or Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
rationales.F06: The negativity for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1) makes Kaposi's sarcoma less likely.
rationales.F11: The poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation is more typical of a benign vascular lesion such as Hemangioma or Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
rationales.F12: The prominent hemosiderin deposits are more typical of a benign vascular lesion such as Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
